To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary protein supply affected growth, feed intake, feed conversion ratio, and muscle development in chickens selected for high breast meat yield and low fatness.

dietary protein supply and selection for increased breast meat and decreased abdominal fatness have a significant effect on the development of the chicken muscle, and on the circulating concentrations of IGF-I.
dietary protein supply influences muscle growth in broiler chickens, and that the effect of dietary protein on muscle growth is genotype dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary protein on muscle development in chickens selected for carcass quality.
the effect of protein supply and selection for improved carcass quality on muscle development and IGF-I and IGF-II levels.
the effect of dietary protein level and line selection for carcass quality on growth, feed efficiency, muscle development, circulating IGF-I and -II, and their relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein restriction reduces growth and muscle development, but the response of the muscle to dietary protein supply depends on the muscle.
the response of muscle growth and development to dietary protein supply depends on the muscle and on the genotype of the chicken.
protein supply has a greater influence on muscle growth and body composition than selection for carcass quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

selection for increased breast yield in chickens resulted in a more efficient use of dietary protein, as evidenced by the lower feed intake and FCR in the selected line, and that this was associated with a greater sensitivity of muscle growth to dietary protein supply.
selection for improved carcass quality has increased muscle deposition and growth rate, which is consistent with the higher circulating concentrations of IGF-I.
selection for improved carcass quality has resulted in an increased muscle mass and proportion of the pectoralis major in broilers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
selection for improved carcass composition in chickens has not compromised the response to dietary protein supply, and that the QL line is less sensitive to dietary protein deficiency.
selection for increased breast yield in broilers is associated with increased muscle growth and circulating IGF-I.
protein supply is an important factor for growth and muscle development in broilers.
